EXTRA_RULES = {k: re.compile(v, re.I) for k, v in EXTRA.items()}

# Tier C on sight: admin, personal, photo dumps, system files, athlete data.
SKIP = [
    ("athlete data", r"dexa|athlete.?snapshot|catapult.?(export|hub)|\bpff\b(?!.*job)|jump.?reports?|[ _]jumps[ _]|bodyweights|completed.?sheets|team.?comp(etition)?\b|testing.?results|\broster\b|combine.?results"),
    ("Eric's own programming archive (2018-19 session sheets)", r"\b(sp|fa)\d\d.?dailys|training outline"),
    ("admin or personal", r"receipt|invoice|payment|paystub|\btax(act|return)?\b|txtag|\buber\b|itinerary|\bresume\b|resume[._ ]|\bcv\b|cover.?letter|coverletter|reference.?letter|recommendation.?letter|\bgmail\b|live assistance|online return|order.?confirm|boarding pass|reservation|\bw-?2\b|\b1099\b|\blease\b|insurance|medical bill|bswhealth|\bvb sign up|master schedule|expense|reimburs|travel.?auth|parking|passport|headshot|business card|job.?(posting|description)|internship.?application|pff part-time|offer letter|\bcontract\b|agenda\b|meeting minutes"),
    ("system or empty", r"(^| )\._|thumbs\.db$|desktop\.ini$|\.ds_store$|\.lnk$|~\$|\.tmp$|\.json$|\.db$|^untitled|\bcopy of copy\b"),
    ("photo or raw video", r"\.(jpe?g|jfif|png|heic|gif|tif|bmp)$|\b(img|dsc|_i2p|vid|mvi|gopr)[_ ]?\d{3,}"),
]
SKIP_RULES = [(k, re.compile(v, re.I)) for k, v in SKIP]

# Eric's own material and the Clemson curriculum: routed to the Phase 1 second pass on
# his method, never onto an outside-source shortlist.
OWN = [
    ("Eric's own team education deck (Phase 1 second pass)", r"07.EDUCATION/TEAM.?EDUCATION|TEAM.EDUCATION.Health|2026.AppliedNewsletter"),
    ("Eric's own playbook material (Phase 1 second pass)", r"SPORT.SCIENCE.PLAYBOOK/BAYLOR VERSION|AP Unit Goal Presentation"),
    ("Eric's own research admin (proposals, committee)", r"04.RESEARCH.*/(02.Proposals|04.Committee|_Archive)/"),
    ("Clemson curriculum (Avedesian), named influence only", r"SPORT.SCIENCE.PLAYBOOK/CLEMSON VERSION"),
    ("Eric's own programming archive (2018-19 From_REMOTE_DESK)", r"^From.REMOTE.DESK/2019 Spring Semester"),
    ("Eric's own course (HHPR 5355, co-taught; Phase 1 material)", r"Academic Courses \(HP5355\)"),
]
OWN_RULES = [(k, re.compile(v, re.I)) for k, v in OWN]


def import_index() -> dict:
    """Map Drive id -> original name, folder, Crossref title, Zotero status, first page."""
    idx: dict = {}
    if not IMPORT.exists():
        print(f"warning: import folder not found: {IMPORT}", file=sys.stderr)
        return idx
    for f in sorted(IMPORT.glob("*.json")):
        try:
            d = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except Exception:
            continue
        items = d if isinstance(d, list) else (list(d.values()) if isinstance(d, dict) else [])
        for r in items:
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            s = r["source"] if isinstance(r.get("source"), dict) else r
            if "id" not in s or "name" not in s:
                continue
            e = idx.setdefault(s["id"], {"name": s["name"], "folder": "", "title": "", "journal": "",
                                         "zotero": "", "first": "", "scholarly": "", "pages": ""})
            if s.get("md5"):
                idx.setdefault("md5:" + s["md5"], e)
            e["folder"] = e["folder"] or (s.get("folder_path") or "")
            e["pages"] = e["pages"] or str(s.get("pages") or "")
            cr = s.get("crossref") if isinstance(s.get("crossref"), dict) else None
            if cr and not e["title"]:
                t = cr.get("title")
                e["title"] = (t[0] if isinstance(t, list) and t else t or "") if t else ""
                j = cr.get("container-title")
                e["journal"] = (j[0] if isinstance(j, list) and j else j or "") if j else ""
            if str(s.get("scholarly")) in ("True", "False") and not e["scholarly"]:
                e["scholarly"] = str(s.get("scholarly"))
    for f in sorted(IMPORT.glob("*.ndjson")):
        for line in f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            try:
                s = json.loads(line)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if isinstance(s, dict) and "id" in s and "name" in s:
                e = idx.setdefault(s["id"], {"name": s["name"], "folder": s.get("folder_path", ""), "title": "",
                                             "journal": "", "zotero": "", "first": "", "scholarly": "",
                                             "pages": str(s.get("pages") or "")})
                if s.get("md5"):
                    idx.setdefault("md5:" + s["md5"], e)
    st = IMPORT / "import-state.json"
    if st.exists():
        for v in json.loads(st.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).values():
            sid = v.get("source_id")
            if sid in idx:
                idx[sid]["zotero"] = v.get("status", "")
                idx[sid]["title"] = idx[sid]["title"] or v.get("title", "")
    for f in sorted(IMPORT.glob("*unresolved*.txt")):
        for block in re.split(r"^### ", f.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), flags=re.M):
            head, _, body = block.partition("\n")
            sid = head.split(" | ")[0].strip()
            if sid in idx and not idx[sid]["first"]:
                idx[sid]["first"] = " ".join(body.split())[:600]
    return idx


LOCAL_ROOTS = {
    "04_RESEARCH": "G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/04_RESEARCH",
    "07_EDUCATION": "G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/07_EDUCATION",
    "09_PRO_DEV": "G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/09_PRO_DEV",
    "AP & Sports Science": "G:/My Drive/Athletic Performance & Sports Science",
    "Research Papers": "G:/My Drive/Research Papers",
}


def extract_first_pages(rows: list, idx: dict) -> None:
    """Write data/first_pages.csv: first ~600 characters of PDFs that have neither a
    descriptive name nor a Crossref title. Reads the local Google Drive copy."""
    from pypdf import PdfReader
    out = DATA / "first_pages.csv"
    have = {}
    if out.exists():
        with open(out, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            have = {r["key"]: r["text"] for r in csv.DictReader(fh)}
    for r in rows:
        key = r["md5"] or r["id"]
        if key in have or r["ext"] != "pdf" or r["source"] not in LOCAL_ROOTS:
            continue
        # Only small files (Drive streams the whole file on read), and only names that
        # say nothing: Drive ids, journal ids, "ContentServer", scanner output.
        stem = r["name"].rsplit(".", 1)[0]
        if int(r["size"] or 0) > 10_000_000 or (len(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]{4,}", stem)) >= 3 and "drive-zotero-import" not in r["path"]):
            continue
        e = idx.get(r["name"].rsplit(".", 1)[0]) or idx.get("md5:" + r["md5"])
        if e and (e["title"] or e["first"]):
            continue
        f = Path(LOCAL_ROOTS[r["source"]]) / r["path"]
        try:
            txt = " ".join((PdfReader(str(f)).pages[0].extract_text() or "").split())[:600]
        except Exception as ex:  # scanned, missing or streamed-only file
            txt = f"(no text: {type(ex).__name__})"
        have[key] = txt or "(no text layer)"
        if len(have) % 50 == 0:
            print("first pages:", len(have), flush=True)
    with open(out, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["key", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows({"key": k, "text": v} for k, v in have.items())


def load_labels() -> dict:
    labels = {}
    # Labels are committed (config/, not data/): they are the one part of this pass a
    # script cannot regenerate.
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(str(ROOT / "config" / "model_labels" / "*.csv"))):
        with open(f, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
                if r.get("key"):
                    labels[r["key"].strip()] = r
    return labels


def default_route(r: dict, discs: list) -> str:
    kind, ext, size = r["kind"], r["ext"], int(r["size"] or 0)
    if r.get("in_zotero") == "True" or r.get("zotero_status") in ("verified", "skipped_existing_pdf"):
        return "already in Zotero"
    if kind in ("video", "audio"):
        return "transcribe"
    if kind == "paper_or_book":
        pages = int(r.get("pages") or 0)
        if ext in ("epub", "mobi") or pages >= 80 or (not pages and size >= 8_000_000):
            return "book"
        return "paper to Zotero"
    if kind in ("document", "slides"):
        return "atomize"
    return "catalog only"


def main() -> None:
    with open(DATA / "unclassified.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    idx = import_index()
    if "--extract" in sys.argv:
        extract_first_pages(rows, idx)
    firsts = {}
    if (DATA / "first_pages.csv").exists():
        with open(DATA / "first_pages.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            firsts = {r["key"]: r["text"] for r in csv.DictReader(fh)}
    labels = load_labels()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        key = r["md5"] or r["id"]
        stem = r["name"].rsplit(".", 1)[0]
        if "drive-zotero-import" in r["path"]:
            e = idx.get(stem)
        else:
            e = idx.get(r["id"]) or idx.get("md5:" + r["md5"])
        orig_name = e["name"] if e and e["name"] != r["name"] else ""
        orig_folder = e["folder"] if e else ""
        pages = e["pages"] if e else ""
        title = (e["title"] if e else "") or r.get("zotero_title", "")
        first = (e["first"] if e else "") or firsts.get(key, "")
        zstat = e["zotero"] if e else ""
        text = " ".join([r["source"], r["path"], orig_folder, orig_name, title]).replace("_", " ")
        rich = text + " " + first
        rr = {**r, "zotero_status": zstat, "pages": pages}
        own = next((k for k, rx in OWN_RULES if rx.search(text)), None)
        how, discs, tier, route, reason = "", [], "", "", ""
        candidate = ""
        lab = labels.get(key)
        # Skip rules look at the file name and its own folder only, so a paper that sits in
        # a folder named "Resume" or a word like "contractile" does not trip them.
        near = " ".join([r["path"].rsplit("/", 2)[-2] if r["path"].count("/") >= 1 else "",
                         orig_name or r["name"]]).replace("_", " ")
        near_ = " ".join([r["path"].rsplit("/", 2)[-2] if r["path"].count("/") >= 1 else "", orig_name or r["name"]])
        skip = next((k for k, rx in SKIP_RULES if rx.search(near) or rx.search(near_)), None)
        if own:
            # Eric's own material wins over a model label: it never goes on an outside-source shortlist.
            how, tier, route, reason = "rule", "B", "own material (Phase 1 second pass)", own
        elif lab:
            how = "model"
            discs = [d.strip() for d in (lab.get("disciplines") or "").split(";") if d.strip()]
            tier, route, reason = lab.get("tier", ""), lab.get("route", ""), lab.get("reason", "")
            candidate = (lab.get("candidate") or "").strip().lower()
        elif skip:
            how, tier, route, reason = "rule", "C", "skip", f"skip rule: {skip}"
        elif own:
            how, tier, route, reason = "rule", "B", "own material (Phase 1 second pass)", own
        else:
            # Rules read the name, folders and Crossref title, not the first page: first
            # pages carry affiliations and abstracts that trip half the keywords.
            discs = [k for k, rx in RULES.items() if rx.search(text)]
            discs += [k for k, rx in EXTRA_RULES.items() if rx.search(text) and k not in discs]
            # More than three hits means the keywords are guessing; send it to the model.
            if 0 < len(discs) <= 3:
                how, tier = "rule", "B"
                route = default_route(rr, discs)
                reason = "keyword rules on " + ("original name, folder and first page" if e else "path and name")
        if how and route != "skip" and zstat in ("verified", "skipped_existing_pdf"):
            route = "already in Zotero"
        out.append({
            "key": key, "source": r["source"], "path": r["path"], "name": r["name"], "ext": r["ext"],
            "kind": r["kind"], "size": r["size"], "pages": pages, "orig_name": orig_name, "orig_folder": orig_folder,
            "title": title, "first_page": first[:300], "zotero_status": zstat, "collections": r["collections"],
            "disciplines": ";".join(discs), "tier": tier, "route": route, "candidate": candidate, "reason": reason, "how": how,
        })
    fields = list(out[0])
    with open(DATA / "triage_model_pass.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    todo = [o for o in out if not o["how"]]
    with open(DATA / "model_todo.csv", "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=fields)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(todo)
    print("rows", len(out), "how", Counter(o["how"] or "todo" for o in out))
    print("tier", Counter(o["tier"] for o in out), "route", Counter(o["route"] for o in out))
    write_summary(out)


def write_summary(out: list) -> None:
    n = len(out)
    how = Counter(o["how"] or "unlabelled" for o in out)
    tiers = Counter(o["tier"] or "unlabelled" for o in out)
    routes = Counter(o["route"] or "unlabelled" for o in out)
    disc = Counter(d for o in out for d in o["disciplines"].split(";") if d)
    lines = [
        "# Flint triage summary (model pass)", "",
        f"Files the keyword rules left unclassified: {n} (`data/unclassified.csv`). "
        f"This pass enriched {sum(1 for o in out if o['orig_folder'] or o['orig_name'] or o['title'])} files "
        "(the Drive-id-named import PDFs, plus other PDFs matched by Drive id or md5) from the June Zotero import logs, "
        "ran extra keyword and skip rules, then Claude labelled the rest in batches from path, "
        "name and first-page text (`config/model_labels/`, committed). Script: `scripts/triage_model_pass.py`. "
        "File-level output: `data/triage_model_pass.csv` (gitignored).", "",
        "## How each file was labelled", "", "| Method | Files |", "|---|---:|",
    ]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in how.most_common()]
    lines += ["", "## By tier", "", "| Tier | Files |", "|---|---:|"]
    names = {"A": "A deep-ingest candidate", "B": "B catalog only", "C": "C skip"}
    lines += [f"| {names.get(k, k)} | {v} |" for k, v in sorted(tiers.items())]
    lines += ["", "## By route", "", "| Route | Files | Tier A |", "|---|---:|---:|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} | {sum(1 for o in out if o['route'] == k and o['tier'] == 'A')} |"
              for k, v in routes.most_common()]
    lines += ["", "## By discipline (tiers A and B)", "",
              "A file can carry several disciplines.", "", "| Discipline | Files | Tier A |", "|---|---:|---:|"]
    for k, _ in disc.most_common():
        sub = [o for o in out if k in o["disciplines"].split(";") and o["tier"] in ("A", "B")]
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {len(sub)} | {sum(o['tier'] == 'A' for o in sub)} |")
    skips = Counter(o["reason"] for o in out if o["tier"] == "C")
    lines += ["", "## Tier C reasons (top 15)", "", "| Reason | Files |", "|---|---:|"]
    lines += [f"| {k} | {v} |" for k, v in skips.most_common(15)]
    (DATA / "triage_model_summary.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

# AGENTS.md

Project: Flint

## What this is
Flint is Claude working as Eric's sport-science, performance, S&C and rehab thought
partner. This repo builds the knowledge base behind that role. It catalogs Eric's
Drive (his own material, TB's Training Info, Landon Evans, courses, papers), routes the
high-value sources into Zotero and the SecondBrain vault, and writes per-discipline
synthesis notes that compare the sources against Eric's own method. It is a side-lane
project, outside the prioritization-slate cap. See `README.md` for the approach and
`docs/PLAN.md` for the checklist.

## Session routine
- Start: run `git pull`, then read docs/STATUS.md before doing anything else.
- End: update docs/STATUS.md (done, next, open questions), commit, and `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions
- Durable notes and decisions go in docs/, committed. Not in chat, not in cloud project docs.
- Documents, data exports, and deliverables live on the primary storage drive (Google Drive 00_Primary_Storage_Drive), not in the repo. Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- `data/` is gitignored except aggregate summaries. Regenerate the file-level manifest with `pwsh scripts/build_manifest.ps1`.
- Codex workers read staged copies in `staging/`, never the Drive root. DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult and PFF exports are never catalogued.
- The ingest review gate has two stages.
  1. Before atomizing, verify the source artifact by an independent route: page order, scanned versus text, transcripts checked against captions.
  2. Before promoting, Codex reviews the staged entries against the staged sources, with instructions to falsify (`staging/review_<source>_codex.md`). Nothing reaches the vault without a GO or a GO AFTER FIXES that has been applied.
- Library entries label every voice. The source author's statements are plain. Eric's judgments get "Eric's review:". The entry writer's own reasoning gets "Inference:". No unlabeled judgments. Every number carries a timestamp or page the reviewer can check, and a claim is only tagged "confirmed in PDF" if that PDF is staged. (Learned from the Harries review, 2026-09-26: 25 of 35 files needed fixes, mostly for attribution.)
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

# Flint triage: label one batch of Drive files

You are labelling files from Eric Rash's Google Drive (Director of Applied Performance,
Baylor Athletics; football sport science) for Flint, his sport-science knowledge base.
Goal: decide which files are worth deep ingest (tier A candidates) and where every file goes.

Input: one CSV (given in your task). Columns: key, source, path, orig_folder, orig_name,
title (Crossref or Zotero title), first_page (first ~300-600 chars of text), pages,
size (bytes), kind, zotero_status.

Output: write exactly one CSV to the path given in your task, UTF-8, header:

    key,disciplines,tier,route,candidate,reason

One row per input row, same keys, no extras, no omissions. Quote fields containing commas.

## Vocabularies (use verbatim)

disciplines: zero or more, separated by ";", from this list only:
Strength and power; Periodization and programming; Speed and sprint; Conditioning and energy systems;
Rehab and return to play; Injury risk and prevention; Load monitoring and GPS; Testing and assessment;
Recovery and sleep; Nutrition and body composition; Anatomy, physiology and biomechanics;
Coaching, skill acquisition and constraints-led approach; Data, technology and reporting;
Leadership, culture and psychology; Female athlete; Youth and development

tier: B (keep, catalog) or C (skip). Never write A; tier A comes from candidate=yes.

route, one of:
- skip: tier C only. Admin, personal, photos, system files, empty, duplicates of nothing useful, athlete data.
- already in Zotero: zotero_status is "verified" or "skipped_existing_pdf".
- paper to Zotero: a journal article, review, or short research report not yet in Zotero.
- book: a book or book-length manual (80+ pages, epub/mobi).
- atomize: a presentation, lecture notes, course material, coach's document or manual whose ideas belong in the vault.
- transcribe: video or audio worth hearing (lectures, talks, podcasts). Raw training footage is skip.
- catalog only: keep a record but no action (templates, spreadsheets of programs, forms, low-value reference).

candidate: yes or no. yes means "this is a deep-ingest candidate Eric should see on a shortlist":
a substantial, idea-dense source from a credible practitioner or researcher (textbook, named coach's
lecture or course, landmark review, conference talk) that would change or sharpen how a
football performance staff trains, monitors, or rehabs athletes. Be selective: in earlier batches
about 6-7% of files were candidates. Generic handouts, single program sheets, marketing and
most individual papers are no (papers go to Zotero in bulk).

reason: one short plain line saying what the file is (author or origin if known). No em dashes.

## Hard rules

1. Athlete data is always C / skip, reason starting "athlete data:". This includes body weights,
   testing results, jump or sprint reports, rosters, DEXA, Catapult or PFF exports, readiness
   sheets, individual athlete files, team spreadsheets of measurements. When unsure whether a
   spreadsheet holds athlete measurements, skip it.
2. Thin evidence never makes a candidate. If there is no title and no first_page text and the
   name is opaque (a Drive id, numbers, "scan", "document"), use B / catalog only / candidate no
   and start the reason with "name only:". You may still route a clearly named PDF from its name.
3. zotero_status verified or skipped_existing_pdf means route "already in Zotero" (unless skip).
4. Eric's own work (his reports, his programs, Baylor internal admin) is not an outside source:
   never candidate=yes. Route his program sheets "catalog only", admin "skip".
5. Do not open or download files. Label from the columns you are given.
6. Do not write anywhere except your one output path.

When done, verify: row count equals input row count, every key present once, every value in
the vocabularies. Report: rows written, tier counts, route counts, candidate count, and a list
of your candidate=yes rows (path + reason).

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# ///
"""Step 2c: draft the tier-A shortlist for each discipline.

    python scripts/build_shortlists.py

Reads data/triage_model_pass.csv (from triage_model_pass.py). A file is on a shortlist
when its tier is A (a model label with candidate=yes). Skipped files and Eric's own
material never appear. Each file is listed once, under its first discipline; the other
disciplines are shown beside it. Writes docs/shortlists/<discipline>.md and the totals
table in docs/shortlists/README.md between the TOTALS markers (the prose around them is
hand-written and kept).
"""
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DATA = ROOT / "data"
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "shortlists"
OWN = "own material (Phase 1 second pass)"
ROUTE_ORDER = ["book", "atomize", "transcribe", "paper to Zotero", "already in Zotero", "catalog only"]


def slug(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s.lower()).strip("-")


def cell(s: str) -> str:
    return (s or "").replace("|", "/").replace("\n", " ").strip()


def main() -> None:
    with open(DATA / "triage_model_pass.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    short = [r for r in rows if r["tier"] == "A" and r["route"] not in ("skip", OWN)]
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    groups: dict = {}
    for r in short:
        discs = [d for d in r["disciplines"].split(";") if d] or ["Unassigned"]
        groups.setdefault(discs[0], []).append((r, discs[1:]))
    for old in OUT.glob("*.md"):
        if old.name != "README.md":
            old.unlink()
    for disc, items in groups.items():
        items.sort(key=lambda x: (ROUTE_ORDER.index(x[0]["route"]) if x[0]["route"] in ROUTE_ORDER else 99,
                                  x[0]["source"], x[0]["path"]))
        lines = [f"# Tier-A shortlist: {disc}", "",
                 f"Draft, {len(items)} files. Generated by `scripts/build_shortlists.py` from the committed "
                 "labels in `config/model_labels/`. Eric approves, strikes or adds; a change is made by "
                 "editing the file's label, then rerunning the two scripts.", "",
                 "| # | Route | What it is | Also | Source | Path | Pages |", "|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---:|"]
        for i, (r, also) in enumerate(items, 1):
            lines.append(f"| {i} | {r['route']} | {cell(r['reason'])} | {cell('; '.join(also))} | "
                         f"{cell(r['source'])} | `{cell(r['path'])}` | {r['pages']} |")
        (OUT / f"{slug(disc)}.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    routes = Counter(r["route"] or "unlabelled" for r in rows)
    tiers = Counter(r["tier"] or "unlabelled" for r in rows)
    t = ["<!-- TOTALS:START (generated by scripts/build_shortlists.py) -->", "",
         f"Files in the model pass: {len(rows)}. Tier A {tiers['A']}, B {tiers['B']}, C {tiers['C']}"
         + (f", unlabelled {tiers['unlabelled']}" if tiers.get("unlabelled") else "") + ".", "",
         "### All files by route", "", "| Route | Files | Tier A |", "|---|---:|---:|"]
    t += [f"| {k} | {v} | {sum(1 for r in rows if r['route'] == k and r['tier'] == 'A')} |"
          for k, v in routes.most_common()]
    t += ["", "### Shortlists", "", "| Discipline | Files | Book | Atomize | Transcribe | Paper | In Zotero | Catalog |",
          "|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
    for disc, items in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
        c = Counter(r["route"] for r, _ in items)
        t.append(f"| [{disc}]({slug(disc)}.md) | {len(items)} | {c['book']} | {c['atomize']} | {c['transcribe']} | "
                 f"{c['paper to Zotero']} | {c['already in Zotero']} | {c['catalog only']} |")
    t += [f"| **Total** | **{len(short)}** | | | | | | |", "", "<!-- TOTALS:END -->"]
    readme = OUT / "README.md"
    body = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if readme.exists() else "# Tier-A shortlists\n\n<!-- TOTALS:START -->\n<!-- TOTALS:END -->\n"
    body = re.sub(r"<!-- TOTALS:START.*?<!-- TOTALS:END -->", lambda _: "\n".join(t), body, flags=re.S)
    readme.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    print("shortlisted", len(short), {k: len(v) for k, v in groups.items()})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Tier-A shortlists (draft, Phase 2)

These are the deep-ingest candidates from the Drive triage, one file per discipline. They are
drafts: nothing here is approved until Eric says so (PLAN Phase 2, last box).

## How they were made

1. `scripts/triage_rules.py`: keyword rules classified 5,693 of 9,702 non-own files. The 3,998
   left over are `data/unclassified.csv`.
2. `scripts/triage_model_pass.py`: enriched those from the June Zotero import logs, ran extra
   keyword and skip rules, then applied Claude's labels (`config/model_labels/batch_*.csv`,
   committed). A label with `candidate=yes` makes the file tier A.
3. An independent reviewer tried to falsify every tier-A label and a random 100 of the skips
   (seed 20260927); its changes were applied as label edits. See the handoff
   `docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-flint-triage.md` for the review record.
4. `scripts/build_shortlists.py`: groups tier A by first discipline and writes these files.

Tier A covers only the files the keyword rules could not place. The 5,693 rule-classified
files carry no tier; the sources already in the queue (`docs/QUEUE.md`: Supertraining,
Bondarchuk, Issurin, Zatsiorsky, Francis, Harries, Old Bull, Landon Evans) were chosen by hand
and are not repeated here. Athlete data and Eric's own material never appear.

To change a shortlist, edit the file's row in `config/model_labels/`, then run
`uv run scripts/triage_model_pass.py` and `uv run scripts/build_shortlists.py`.

## Totals

<!-- TOTALS:START -->
<!-- TOTALS:END -->

## Throughput estimate

Observed ingest rate (STATUS, 2026-09-26 to 09-28): about 269 vault entries from 6 sources by
the end of day 2, then 68 entries from 4 chapter batches on day 3. Each batch needs an atomizer
pass plus one or two independent review rounds, so a working session clears about 3 to 4
chapter-sized batches (roughly 60 to 70 entries).

Read that against the shortlist by route:
- **Books:** a book is about 5 to 10 chapter batches, so 1 to 3 sessions each. Books are the
  bottleneck; pick a handful per discipline, not all.
- **Atomize (decks, lectures, manuals):** most are one batch each, so 3 to 4 per session.
- **Transcribe:** one background job at a time on the laptop (memory limit), about as long as
  the audio, then an atomize batch. Overnight on the Mac is faster.
- **Papers (to Zotero or already in Zotero):** bulk import is cheap; a paper only costs a
  session slot if it gets a Paper Brief.

At 3 to 4 batches per session, a shortlist in the low hundreds is several months of side-lane
sessions. Approving means choosing an order, not only a yes.

## Decisions for Eric

1. **Approve each discipline's shortlist:** strike, add, or reorder. The first-ranked
   disciplines should follow PLAN Phase 4 (rehab and RTP first, then speed, strength,
   conditioning, load monitoring, recovery, nutrition).
2. **Papers already in Zotero:** do tier-A papers that are already in Zotero count as atomize
   targets (a vault entry), or only as Paper Briefs through the Zotero queue?
3. **Books versus the queue:** do shortlisted books join `docs/QUEUE.md` after the current
   queue (Supertraining Ch4-9, Bondarchuk, Zatsiorsky, Francis), or can one jump it?
4. **Mike Golden library (1,245 files):** same priority as TB and Landon? (open in STATUS)
5. **Rule-classified files:** the 5,693 files the keyword rules placed were never screened for
   tier A. Run a candidate pass on them next, or leave them at catalog level?
6. **Jev pilot:** these labels were made without Jev. The preregistered pilot
   (`TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/DRIVE_TRIAGE_PREREG.md`) still needs its answer key; it can now be
   scored against these labels only after the blind answer key exists.

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# ///
"""Step 2c: draft the tier-A shortlist for each discipline.

    python scripts/build_shortlists.py

Reads data/triage_model_pass.csv (from triage_model_pass.py). A file is on a shortlist
when its tier is A (a model label with candidate=yes). Skipped files and Eric's own
material never appear. Each file is listed once, under its first discipline; the other
disciplines are shown beside it. Writes docs/shortlists/<discipline>.md and the totals
table in docs/shortlists/README.md between the TOTALS markers (the prose around them is
hand-written and kept).
"""
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
DATA = ROOT / "data"
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "shortlists"
OWN = "own material (Phase 1 second pass)"
ROUTE_ORDER = ["book", "atomize", "transcribe", "paper to Zotero", "already in Zotero", "catalog only"]


def slug(s: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", s.lower()).strip("-")


def cell(s: str) -> str:
    return (s or "").replace("|", "/").replace("\n", " ").strip()


def main() -> None:
    with open(DATA / "triage_model_pass.csv", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    short = [r for r in rows if r["tier"] == "A" and r["route"] not in ("skip", OWN)]
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    groups: dict = {}
    for r in short:
        discs = [d for d in r["disciplines"].split(";") if d] or ["Unassigned"]
        groups.setdefault(discs[0], []).append((r, discs[1:]))
    for old in OUT.glob("*.md"):
        if old.name != "README.md":
            old.unlink()
    for disc, items in groups.items():
        items.sort(key=lambda x: (ROUTE_ORDER.index(x[0]["route"]) if x[0]["route"] in ROUTE_ORDER else 99,
                                  x[0]["source"], x[0]["path"]))
        lines = [f"# Tier-A shortlist: {disc}", "",
                 f"Draft, {len(items)} files. Generated by `scripts/build_shortlists.py` from the committed "
                 "labels in `config/model_labels/`. Eric approves, strikes or adds; a change is made by "
                 "editing the file's label, then rerunning the two scripts.", "",
                 "| # | Route | What it is | Also | Source | Path | Pages |", "|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---:|"]
        for i, (r, also) in enumerate(items, 1):
            lines.append(f"| {i} | {r['route']} | {cell(r['reason'])} | {cell('; '.join(also))} | "
                         f"{cell(r['source'])} | `{cell(r['path'])}` | {r['pages']} |")
        (OUT / f"{slug(disc)}.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    routes = Counter(r["route"] or "unlabelled" for r in rows)
    tiers = Counter(r["tier"] or "unlabelled" for r in rows)
    t = ["<!-- TOTALS:START (generated by scripts/build_shortlists.py) -->", "",
         f"Files in the model pass: {len(rows)}. Tier A {tiers['A']}, B {tiers['B']}, C {tiers['C']}"
         + (f", unlabelled {tiers['unlabelled']}" if tiers.get("unlabelled") else "") + ".", "",
         "### All files by route", "", "| Route | Files | Tier A |", "|---|---:|---:|"]
    t += [f"| {k} | {v} | {sum(1 for r in rows if r['route'] == k and r['tier'] == 'A')} |"
          for k, v in routes.most_common()]
    t += ["", "### Shortlists", "", "| Discipline | Files | Book | Atomize | Transcribe | Paper | In Zotero | Catalog |",
          "|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|"]
    for disc, items in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
        c = Counter(r["route"] for r, _ in items)
        t.append(f"| [{disc}]({slug(disc)}.md) | {len(items)} | {c['book']} | {c['atomize']} | {c['transcribe']} | "
                 f"{c['paper to Zotero']} | {c['already in Zotero']} | {c['catalog only']} |")
    t += [f"| **Total** | **{len(short)}** | | | | | | |", "", "<!-- TOTALS:END -->"]
    readme = OUT / "README.md"
    body = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if readme.exists() else "# Tier-A shortlists\n\n<!-- TOTALS:START -->\n<!-- TOTALS:END -->\n"
    body = re.sub(r"<!-- TOTALS:START.*?<!-- TOTALS:END -->", lambda _: "\n".join(t), body, flags=re.S)
    readme.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    print("shortlisted", len(short), {k: len(v) for k, v in groups.items()})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

                 f"Draft, {len(items)} files. Generated by `scripts/build_shortlists.py` from the committed "

    t = ["<!-- TOTALS:START (generated by scripts/build_shortlists.py) -->", "",

    t += ["", "### Shortlists", "", "| Discipline | Files | Book | Atomize | Transcribe | Paper | In Zotero | Catalog |",

    for disc, items in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):

    nq = sum(1 for r in short if QUEUED.search(" ".join([r["path"], r["orig_name"], orig.get(r["key"], ""), r["reason"]])))

    body = re.sub(r"<!-- TOTALS:START.*?<!-- TOTALS:END -->", lambda _: "\n".join(t), body, flags=re.S)

# Tier-A shortlists (draft, Phase 2)

These are the deep-ingest candidates from the Drive triage, one file per discipline. They are
drafts: nothing here is approved until Eric says so (PLAN Phase 2, last box).

## How they were made

1. `scripts/triage_rules.py`: keyword rules classified 5,693 of 9,702 non-own files. The 3,998
   left over are `data/unclassified.csv`.
2. `scripts/triage_model_pass.py`: enriched those from the June Zotero import logs, ran extra
   keyword and skip rules, then applied Claude's labels (`config/model_labels/batch_*.csv`,
   committed). A label with `candidate=yes` makes the file tier A.
3. An independent reviewer tried to falsify every tier-A label and a random 100 of the skips
   (seed 20260927); its changes were applied as label edits. See the handoff
   `docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-flint-triage.md` for the review record.
4. `scripts/build_shortlists.py`: groups tier A by first discipline and writes these files.

Tier A covers only the files the keyword rules could not place. The 5,693 rule-classified
files carry no tier; the sources already in the queue (`docs/QUEUE.md`: Supertraining,
Bondarchuk, Issurin, Zatsiorsky, Francis, Harries, Old Bull, Landon Evans) were chosen by hand
and are not repeated here. Athlete data and Eric's own material never appear.

To change a shortlist, edit the file's row in `config/model_labels/`, then run
`uv run scripts/triage_model_pass.py` and `uv run scripts/build_shortlists.py`.

## Totals

Observed ingest rate (STATUS, 2026-09-26 to 09-28): about 269 vault entries from 6 sources by
the end of day 2, then 68 entries from 4 chapter batches on day 3. Each batch needs an atomizer
pass plus one or two independent review rounds, so a working session clears about 3 to 4
chapter-sized batches (roughly 60 to 70 entries).

- **Books:** a book is about 5 to 10 chapter batches, so 1 to 3 sessions each. Books are the
  bottleneck; pick a handful per discipline, not all.
- **Atomize (decks, lectures, manuals):** most are one batch each, so 3 to 4 per session.
- **Transcribe:** one background job at a time on the laptop (memory limit), about as long as
  the audio, then an atomize batch. Overnight on the Mac is faster.
- **Papers (to Zotero or already in Zotero):** bulk import is cheap; a paper only costs a
  session slot if it gets a Paper Brief.

At 3 to 4 batches per session, a shortlist in the low hundreds is several months of side-lane
sessions. Approving means choosing an order, not only a yes.

   disciplines should follow PLAN Phase 4 (rehab and RTP first, then speed, strength,

   targets (a vault entry), or only as Paper Briefs through the Zotero queue?

   queue (Supertraining Ch4-9, Bondarchuk, Zatsiorsky, Francis), or can one jump it?

   (`TypeSafe_Sandbox/docs/DRIVE_TRIAGE_PREREG.md`) still needs its answer key; it can now be
   scored against these labels only after the blind answer key exists.

These are the deep-ingest candidates from the Drive triage, one file per discipline. They are
drafts: nothing here is approved until Eric says so (PLAN Phase 2, last box).

   left over are `data/unclassified.csv`.

   `docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-flint-triage.md` for the review record.

files carry no tier. Sources already in `docs/QUEUE.md` or the vault (Supertraining,
Bondarchuk, Issurin, Zatsiorsky, Francis, Verkhoshansky, Harries, Old Bull, Landon Evans) stay on

batches 01-08, 11 and 12. This session finished the labelling, ran the reviews and drafted
the shortlists.

## Done
- **All 3,998 files the keyword rules left unclassified are labelled.**

  - Totals: `data/triage_model_summary.md` and `docs/shortlists/README.md`.
- **Label files** (committed, in `config/model_labels/`):
  - `batch_01-08, 11, 12`: the old session's labellers. Batch 12 was unverified; it was reviewed here.

  - A label with candidate=yes and route other than skip becomes tier A. Before, tier A was always 0.
  - The docstring now gives the right label path.
  - The athlete-data skip rule now catches `bodyweight` and `BW`.
  - Five 2019 team bodyweight sheets were relabelled C (athlete data) in `batch_11.csv`.
- **Shortlists:** `scripts/build_shortlists.py` (new) writes `docs/shortlists/<discipline>.md` and the
  README totals.

## Review record (gate for this pass)
| Round | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Batches 01-12: all 141 candidates plus 100 random skips (seed 20260927) | 96 changes. 74 candidates dropped (single papers, commercial ebooks, thin evidence, off-topic, colleagues' talks); 13 skips reversed to catalog only; 0 athlete data. 41% of candidates kept as-is. 2 changes rejected by the orchestrator (the SP19 "DAILYS" sheets stay under their own skip rule). |
| 2 | The 94 applied round-1 fixes | GO AFTER FIXES. 90 confirmed, 6 adjusted: "Vertical Foundations" restored, the Panther off-site packet dropped, *Under the Bar* routed book, the "IA Assessment Manual is Eric's own" claim not shown, *Legacy* candidacy moved from a 0-byte copy to a real copy. | 1b | Batches 14-16: 28 candidates, all 75 skips, 60 sampled tier-B books, decks and lectures | 37 changes. 7 candidates dropped, 2 added (Joyce and Lewindon; Golden *Blueprint*), 10 skips reversed, 8 duplicate groups. 68% of candidates kept as-is. *The Manual* Vol 1 replaces Vol 3 as the series candidate. |
| Final | Orchestrator dedup | Second copies of *High-Performance Training for Sports* and Viru catalogued. |

# Tier-A shortlists (draft, Phase 2)

These are the deep-ingest candidates from the Drive triage, one file per discipline. They are
drafts: nothing here is approved until Eric says so (PLAN Phase 2, last box).

## How they were made

1. `scripts/triage_rules.py`: keyword rules classified 5,693 of 9,702 non-own files. The 3,998
   left over are `data/unclassified.csv`.
2. `scripts/triage_model_pass.py`: enriched those from the June Zotero import logs, ran extra
   keyword and skip rules, then applied Claude's labels (`config/model_labels/batch_*.csv`,
   committed). A label with `candidate=yes` makes the file tier A.
3. An independent reviewer tried to falsify every tier-A label and a random 100 of the skips
   (seed 20260927); its changes were applied as label edits. See the handoff
   `docs/handoffs/2026-09-28-flint-triage.md` for the review record.
4. `scripts/build_shortlists.py`: groups tier A by first discipline and writes these files.

Tier A covers only the files the keyword rules could not place. The 5,693 rule-classified
files carry no tier. Sources already in `docs/QUEUE.md` or the vault (Supertraining,
Bondarchuk, Issurin, Zatsiorsky, Francis, Verkhoshansky, Harries, Old Bull, Landon Evans) stay on
the lists with Queue = yes, so they are not scheduled twice. Athlete data and Eric's own
material never appear.

The review files (`zz_review_*.csv` in `config/model_labels/`) override the batch labels; the
"Review note" column shows why a label changed.

To change a shortlist, edit the file's row in `config/model_labels/`, then run
`uv run scripts/triage_model_pass.py` and `uv run scripts/build_shortlists.py`.

## Totals

<!-- TOTALS:START (generated by scripts/build_shortlists.py) -->

Files in the model pass: 3998. Tier A 88, B 2329, C 1581.

## Throughput estimate

Observed ingest rate (STATUS, 2026-09-26 to 09-28): about 269 vault entries from 6 sources by
the end of day 2, then 68 entries from 4 chapter batches on day 3. Each batch needs an atomizer
pass plus one or two independent review rounds, so a working session clears about 3 to 4
chapter-sized batches (roughly 60 to 70 entries).

Read that against the shortlist by route:
- **Books:** a book is about 5 to 10 chapter batches, so 1 to 3 sessions each. Books are the
  bottleneck; pick a handful per discipline, not all.
- **Atomize (decks, lectures, manuals):** most are one batch each, so 3 to 4 per session.
- **Transcribe:** one background job at a time on the laptop (memory limit), about as long as
  the audio, then an atomize batch. Overnight on the Mac is faster.
- **Papers (to Zotero or already in Zotero):** bulk import is cheap; a paper only costs a
  session slot if it gets a Paper Brief.

# Flint handoff: Phase 2 triage (2026-09-28)

Branch `step1-triage`. The first triage agent (old session) was stopped mid-run after
batches 01-08, 11 and 12. This session finished the labelling, ran the reviews and drafted
the shortlists.

## Done
- **All 3,998 files the keyword rules left unclassified are labelled.**
  - 1,360 files are labelled by rule and 2,638 by model.
  - Tiers: A 88, B 2,329, C 1,581.
  - Totals: `data/triage_model_summary.md` and `docs/shortlists/README.md`.
- **Label files** (committed, in `config/model_labels/`):
  - `batch_01-08, 11, 12`: the old session's labellers. Batch 12 was unverified; it was reviewed here.
  - `batch_14-16`: the 483 rows still open, labelled this session from `data/_tmp/todo_batch_*.csv`.
    Brief: `docs/triage-label-brief.md`: vocabularies, candidate bar and hard rules. Reuse it for any relabel or Jev comparison.
  - `zz_review_*.csv`: review overrides. The loader reads files in sorted order, so later files win.
- **Script changes** (`scripts/triage_model_pass.py`):
  - A label with candidate=yes and route other than skip becomes tier A. Before, tier A was always 0.
  - The docstring now gives the right label path.
  - The athlete-data skip rule now catches `bodyweight` and `BW`.
  - Five 2019 team bodyweight sheets were relabelled C (athlete data) in `batch_11.csv`.
- **Shortlists:** `scripts/build_shortlists.py` (new) writes `docs/shortlists/<discipline>.md` and the
  README totals.
  - 88 files across 14 disciplines. 12 are already in the queue or vault (flagged Queue), so 76 are new.

# Drive triage: pre-registration

Tenth item measured against the capability map. Registered 2026-09-26, **before any
model call**. The registering commit is the one that adds this file. Bars approved by
Eric on 2026-09-26. Consumer: the Flint project (`erash11/Flint`), which builds Eric's
sport-science knowledge base from his Drive.

**Governance: tier A.** The state is a Drive folder path, a file name, and up to 2,000
characters of a document's first page. The documents are coaching and research
material: books, papers, course handouts and slides. No athlete data. Flint's catalog
excludes DexaProject, athlete snapshots, Catapult and PFF exports before anything
reaches this test.

## Question

Can Jev put the Drive files that Flint's keyword rules cannot place into the Zotero
taxonomy (14 domains, 96 topics, `zotero_classify/taxonomy.py`), confidently enough
that Flint can route them without a person reading each one?

## Gate check (capability map, three conditions)

1. **Genuinely fuzzy.** Deciding a coaching PDF's domain from its folder, name and
   first page is not a join, a threshold or a lookup.
2. **A consumer exists.** Flint routes every file by domain: into Zotero, the vault,
   the book queue or the transcription queue. It also builds a per-domain shortlist
   of files to ingest in full.
3. **Code baseline measured first.** Flint's keyword rules (`Flint/scripts/triage_rules.py`)
   classified 5,714 of 9,712 non-report files (59%). An md5 match against Zotero's
   Drive attachment store placed 81 more. The model pass covers only what code leaves.

## Sample (committed here: `drive_triage/sample.csv`)

200 files drawn by `Flint/scripts/draw_jev_sample.py`, seed 20260926, before any call.

- 100 from the 3,548 files the rules could not classify.
- 100 from the 5,254 files the rules did classify. These also measure the rules' own
  precision.
- Each half is stratified by source root, with proportional allocation.
- Excluded: Eric's own reports and dashboards, images, archives, and files already in
  Zotero.

## State per file

Folder path, file name, and the Zotero title where the md5 match recovered one. For
PDFs, Word files and slides, add up to 2,000 characters of first-page text. Video and
audio send path and name only. Files that are not synced locally (TB's Training Info)
are fetched with `gws` into a gitignored staging folder. State is built by code before
the answer key is written, and it is identical for every model.

## Questions

1. **Topic.** The `zotero_classify` topic Choice, unchanged (`classify.question()`),
   with the same domain fallback.
2. **Route.** One new Choice:
   - a research paper
   - a book or book chapter
   - course or lecture material
   - a coaching resource (programs, drills, templates, presentations)
   - Eric's own work
   - not sport-science material

## Answer key

Claude labels all 200 (domain, topic, route) from the same state, blind to every
model's answers, before the first Jev call. The labels are committed before Jev runs.

## Comparators (same 200, same state, same taxonomy)

- Flint's keyword rules, already run. On the unclassified half they count as misses.
- Haiku: one call per file, forced to name a topic.
- Codex: the same.

## Bars (fixed here; they never move)

| Measure | Bar |
|---|---|
| Jev confident: topic probability at or above the measured 0.50 cut | at least 60% of the 200 (120 files) |
| Jev domain accuracy on its confident answers, against the answer key | at least 90% |
| Jev versus Haiku: domain accuracy on Jev's confident subset | Jev at least equal to Haiku |
| Cost for the 200 | reported, no bar |

**Pass requires all three bars.** Topic-level and route accuracy are reported without
bars. The answer key comes before the models run, and the models do not define it.

## Answer-key audit (required step, capability map 2026-09-26)

Pull every file where Jev clears the 0.50 cut and its domain differs from the answer
key. Eric judges them blind: shuffled, sides hidden, input and the two answers only.
He sees at most 20 (a random 20 if there are more). The score on the original labels
decides pass or fail; the audited score is reported next to it.

## Outcomes

- **Pass.** Jev runs on Flint's remaining unclassified files. Below-cut answers fall
  back to domain, and anything still ambiguous goes to Claude.
- **Fail.** The best comparator does the pass. The result is written up here as the
  tenth entry on the map.

# /// script

"""Draw the 200-file sample for the pre-registered Jev triage test.

    uv run scripts/draw_jev_sample.py

100 files the keyword rules could not classify plus 100 they did, each half
stratified by source root with proportional allocation (largest remainder), seed
fixed. Excludes Eric's own reports, images, archives and files already in Zotero
(those already carry a Jev topic from zotero_classify). Writes data/jev_sample.csv.
The sample is drawn once, before any model call, and committed with the
pre-registration.
"""
import csv
import random
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

SEED = 20260926
PER_HALF = 100
DATA = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data"
EXCLUDE_ROUTES = {"Eric's reports (archive)", "already in Zotero"}
EXCLUDE_KINDS = {"image", "archive"}


def stratified(rows: list[dict], n: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[dict]:
    by_source = defaultdict(list)
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["id"]):  # stable order before shuffling
        by_source[r["source"]].append(r)

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Classify the Zotero library into the taxonomy, backing off when unsure.
3	
4	One `Choice` question per record over all 89 topics. The answer carries `confidence`,
5	and that one number decides how specific an answer we report:
6	
7	    confidence >= CONFIDENT   ->  report the topic
8	    confidence <  CONFIDENT   ->  report the DOMAIN that topic sits in
9	
10	Nothing is dropped and nothing is sent for review. A record the model cannot place
11	precisely still comes back with a true, useful, coarser label. That only works because
12	`topic -> domain` is a strict function in taxonomy.py.
13	
14	Every raw response is written to JSONL, probabilities included, before any threshold
15	is applied. Two reasons: a crash at record 900 must not cost 900 calls, and the
16	threshold is then a sweep over saved data rather than something to re-measure.
17	
18	    python classify.py --limit 40 --out runs/sample.jsonl
19	    python classify.py --out runs/full.jsonl              # all 1,418
20	    python classify.py --out runs/full.jsonl --report     # re-read, no calls
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	import argparse
26	import json
27	import sys
28	import time
29	from collections import Counter
30	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
31	from pathlib import Path
32	
33	import jev_client
34	import library
35	import taxonomy
36	
37	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
38	
39	# Measured on 41 hand-labelled records (validate.py), NOT inherited.
40	#
41	# The cookbook uses 0.90 for SEC filings, where the answers it was unsure about were
42	# only 40% right, so backing off bought a lot. Here the unsure answers are mostly
43	# still right - forced to name a topic every time, it gets 36 of 41 - so a high cutoff
44	# gives up precision for nothing. Measured across the sweep, the SAME two records are
45	# wrong at every cutoff from 0.50 up; all a higher cutoff does is convert correct
46	# topics into correct-but-coarser domains.
47	#
48	#   cutoff 0.90 (cookbook)  ->  15 exact topics, 24 domains, 2 wrong
49	#   cutoff 0.50 (ours)      ->  33 exact topics,  6 domains, 2 wrong
50	#
51	# Below 0.50 the error count rises (4 at 0.45, 5 at 0.30), so 0.50 is the knee: the
52	# most precision available for the smallest error budget.
53	CONFIDENT = 0.50
54	
55	QUESTION = (
56	    "Which single topic is this research record mainly about? Judge the work itself "
57	    "as its title and abstract describe it, not the field it loosely belongs to."
58	)
59	
60	# 1,200 requests/minute is the documented ceiling. Eight workers against ~0.3s calls
61	# is nowhere near it, and leaves the machine responsive.
62	WORKERS = 8
63	
64	
65	def question() -> dict:
66	    return {
67	        "topic": {
68	            "type": "choice",
69	            "instructions": QUESTION,
70	            "criteria": dict(taxonomy.CRITERIA),
71	        }
72	    }
73	
74	
75	def classify_one(record: dict, key: str) -> dict:
76	    """One record -> one saved row. Raises only what the caller should record."""
77	    started = time.monotonic()
78	    answers = jev_client.system_one(
79	        library.state_for(record), question(), key, timeout=20.0
80	    )
81	    answer = answers.get("topic")
82	    if not isinstance(answer, dict):
83	        raise jev_client.JevError("no topic answer")
84	    topic = answer.get("choice")
85	    confidence = answer.get("confidence")
86	    probabilities = answer.get("probabilities") or {}
87	    if topic not in taxonomy.DOMAIN_OF:
88	        raise jev_client.JevError(f"answer outside the taxonomy: {topic!r}")
89	    if not isinstance(confidence, (int, float)):
90	        raise jev_client.JevError("no confidence on the answer")
91	
92	    # Keep only the head of the distribution. All 89 probabilities per record would
93	    # be ~1.2MB of mostly zeroes across the library, and the tail answers nothing.
94	    top = sorted(probabilities.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:5]
95	    return {
96	        "item_key": record["item_key"],
97	        "title": record["title"],
98	        "has_abstract": record["has_abstract"],
99	        "topic": topic,
100	        "domain": taxonomy.domain_of(topic),
101	        "confidence": round(float(confidence), 4),
102	        "top": [[name, round(float(p), 4)] for name, p in top],
103	        "ms": int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
104	    }
105	
106	
107	def report(rows: list[dict], confident: float = CONFIDENT) -> None:
108	    """What the run actually produced, split by the stratum that matters."""
109	    if not rows:
110	        print("no rows")
111	        return
112	
113	    def resolve(row: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
114	        if row["confidence"] >= confident:
115	            return "topic", row["topic"]
116	        return "domain", row["domain"]
117	
118	    print(f"\n{len(rows)} records classified at a {confident:.2f} cutoff")
119	    for label, subset in (
120	        ("all", rows),
121	        ("with abstract", [r for r in rows if r["has_abstract"]]),
122	        ("title only", [r for r in rows if not r["has_abstract"]]),
123	    ):
124	        if not subset:
125	            continue
126	        precise = sum(1 for r in subset if resolve(r)[0] == "topic")
127	        mean = sum(r["confidence"] for r in subset) / len(subset)
128	        print(f"  {label:<14} {len(subset):>5}   "
129	              f"named a topic {precise / len(subset):>5.1%}   "
130	              f"mean confidence {mean:.2f}")
131	
132	    print("\nrecords per domain (after backoff):")
133	    domains = Counter(r["domain"] for r in rows)
134	    for domain, count in domains.most_common():
135	        junk = "  <- junk" if domain == taxonomy.JUNK_DOMAIN else ""
136	        print(f"  {count:>5}  {domain}{junk}")
137	
138	    unused = sorted(set(taxonomy.TOPICS) - {r["topic"] for r in rows})
139	    if unused:
140	        print(f"\n{len(unused)} topics never chosen: {', '.join(unused[:12])}"
141	              + (" ..." if len(unused) > 12 else ""))
142	
143	
144	def load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
145	    if not path.exists():
146	        return []
147	    rows = []
148	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
149	        line = line.strip()
150	        if not line:
151	            continue
152	        try:
153	            rows.append(json.loads(line))
154	        except ValueError:
155	            continue  # a torn final line from an interrupted run
156	    return rows
157	
158	
159	def main() -> int:
160	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
161	    parser.add_argument("--out", default="runs/full.jsonl")
162	    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="first N records only")
163	    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=WORKERS)
164	    parser.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=CONFIDENT)
165	    parser.add_argument("--report", action="store_true",
166	                        help="summarise an existing run, make no calls")
167	    args = parser.parse_args()
168	
169	    out_path = Path(args.out)
170	    if not out_path.is_absolute():
171	        out_path = HERE / out_path
172	    existing = load(out_path)
173	
174	    if args.report:
175	        report(existing, args.threshold)
176	        return 0
177	
178	    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
179	    done = {row["item_key"] for row in existing}
180	    records = library.records()
181	    if args.limit:
182	        records = records[:args.limit]
183	    todo = [r for r in records if r["item_key"] not in done]
184	
185	    print(f"{len(records)} records in scope, {len(done)} already done, "
186	          f"{len(todo)} to do")
187	    if not todo:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Classify the Zotero library into the taxonomy, backing off when unsure.

One `Choice` question per record over all 89 topics. The answer carries `confidence`,
and that one number decides how specific an answer we report:

    confidence >= CONFIDENT   ->  report the topic
    confidence <  CONFIDENT   ->  report the DOMAIN that topic sits in

Nothing is dropped and nothing is sent for review. A record the model cannot place
precisely still comes back with a true, useful, coarser label. That only works because
`topic -> domain` is a strict function in taxonomy.py.

Every raw response is written to JSONL, probabilities included, before any threshold
is applied. Two reasons: a crash at record 900 must not cost 900 calls, and the
threshold is then a sweep over saved data rather than something to re-measure.

    python classify.py --limit 40 --out runs/sample.jsonl
    python classify.py --out runs/full.jsonl              # all 1,418
    python classify.py --out runs/full.jsonl --report     # re-read, no calls
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import jev_client
import library
import taxonomy

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# Measured on 41 hand-labelled records (validate.py), NOT inherited.
#
# The cookbook uses 0.90 for SEC filings, where the answers it was unsure about were
# only 40% right, so backing off bought a lot. Here the unsure answers are mostly
# still right - forced to name a topic every time, it gets 36 of 41 - so a high cutoff
# gives up precision for nothing. Measured across the sweep, the SAME two records are
# wrong at every cutoff from 0.50 up; all a higher cutoff does is convert correct
# topics into correct-but-coarser domains.
#
#   cutoff 0.90 (cookbook)  ->  15 exact topics, 24 domains, 2 wrong
#   cutoff 0.50 (ours)      ->  33 exact topics,  6 domains, 2 wrong
#
# Below 0.50 the error count rises (4 at 0.45, 5 at 0.30), so 0.50 is the knee: the
# most precision available for the smallest error budget.
CONFIDENT = 0.50

QUESTION = (
    "Which single topic is this research record mainly about? Judge the work itself "
    "as its title and abstract describe it, not the field it loosely belongs to."
)

# 1,200 requests/minute is the documented ceiling. Eight workers against ~0.3s calls
# is nowhere near it, and leaves the machine responsive.
WORKERS = 8


def question() -> dict:
    return {
        "topic": {
            "type": "choice",
            "instructions": QUESTION,
            "criteria": dict(taxonomy.CRITERIA),
        }
    }


def classify_one(record: dict, key: str) -> dict:
    """One record -> one saved row. Raises only what the caller should record."""
    started = time.monotonic()
    answers = jev_client.system_one(
        library.state_for(record), question(), key, timeout=20.0
    )
    answer = answers.get("topic")
    if not isinstance(answer, dict):
        raise jev_client.JevError("no topic answer")
    topic = answer.get("choice")
    confidence = answer.get("confidence")
    probabilities = answer.get("probabilities") or {}
    if topic not in taxonomy.DOMAIN_OF:
        raise jev_client.JevError(f"answer outside the taxonomy: {topic!r}")
    if not isinstance(confidence, (int, float)):
        raise jev_client.JevError("no confidence on the answer")

    # Keep only the head of the distribution. All 89 probabilities per record would
    # be ~1.2MB of mostly zeroes across the library, and the tail answers nothing.
    top = sorted(probabilities.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:5]
    return {
        "item_key": record["item_key"],
        "title": record["title"],
        "has_abstract": record["has_abstract"],
        "topic": topic,
        "domain": taxonomy.domain_of(topic),
        "confidence": round(float(confidence), 4),
        "top": [[name, round(float(p), 4)] for name, p in top],
        "ms": int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
    }


def report(rows: list[dict], confident: float = CONFIDENT) -> None:
    """What the run actually produced, split by the stratum that matters."""
    if not rows:
        print("no rows")
        return

    def resolve(row: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
        if row["confidence"] >= confident:
            return "topic", row["topic"]
        return "domain", row["domain"]

    print(f"\n{len(rows)} records classified at a {confident:.2f} cutoff")
    for label, subset in (
        ("all", rows),
        ("with abstract", [r for r in rows if r["has_abstract"]]),
        ("title only", [r for r in rows if not r["has_abstract"]]),
    ):
        if not subset:
            continue
        precise = sum(1 for r in subset if resolve(r)[0] == "topic")
        mean = sum(r["confidence"] for r in subset) / len(subset)
        print(f"  {label:<14} {len(subset):>5}   "
              f"named a topic {precise / len(subset):>5.1%}   "
              f"mean confidence {mean:.2f}")

    print("\nrecords per domain (after backoff):")
    domains = Counter(r["domain"] for r in rows)
    for domain, count in domains.most_common():
        junk = "  <- junk" if domain == taxonomy.JUNK_DOMAIN else ""
        print(f"  {count:>5}  {domain}{junk}")

    unused = sorted(set(taxonomy.TOPICS) - {r["topic"] for r in rows})
    if unused:
        print(f"\n{len(unused)} topics never chosen: {', '.join(unused[:12])}"
              + (" ..." if len(unused) > 12 else ""))


def load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    rows = []
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            rows.append(json.loads(line))
        except ValueError:
            continue  # a torn final line from an interrupted run
    return rows


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="runs/full.jsonl")
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="first N records only")
    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=WORKERS)
    parser.add_argument("--threshold", type=float, default=CONFIDENT)
    parser.add_argument("--report", action="store_true",
                        help="summarise an existing run, make no calls")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    out_path = Path(args.out)
    if not out_path.is_absolute():
        out_path = HERE / out_path
    existing = load(out_path)

    if args.report:
        report(existing, args.threshold)
        return 0

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    done = {row["item_key"] for row in existing}
    records = library.records()
    if args.limit:
        records = records[:args.limit]
    todo = [r for r in records if r["item_key"] not in done]

    print(f"{len(records)} records in scope, {len(done)} already done, "
          f"{len(todo)} to do")
    if not todo:
        report(existing, args.threshold)
        return 0

    key = jev_client.api_key()
    failures: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    written = 0
    started = time.monotonic()

    # Append as each result lands. An interrupted run resumes from the file.
    with out_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) as pool:
            def work(record: dict):
                try:
                    return record, classify_one(record, key), None
                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                    return record, None, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"

            for record, row, error in pool.map(work, todo):
                if error:
                    failures.append((record["item_key"], error))
                    continue
                handle.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
                written += 1
                if written % 100 == 0:
                    handle.flush()
                    rate = written / (time.monotonic() - started)
                    print(f"  {written}/{len(todo)}  ({rate:.1f}/s)")

    elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
    print(f"\nwrote {written} rows to {out_path} in {elapsed:.0f}s")
    if failures:
        print(f"{len(failures)} failed (rerun to retry; finished rows are skipped):")
        for item_key, error in failures[:8]:
            print(f"  {item_key}  {error}")
        if len(failures) > 8:
            print(f"  ... and {len(failures) - 8} more")

    report(load(out_path), args.threshold)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal bounded client for the TypeSafe System One endpoint. Stdlib only.

Lifted from the skill router's `ask()`, which is the only HTTP path in this repo that
has been reviewed. The important property is the same here even though a batch job is
not latency-critical: **the timeout is real wall-clock time, not a socket timeout.**

`urlopen(timeout=)` bounds each individual blocking operation, so DNS, connect, TLS
and every body read each get the full value; a server trickling bytes never trips it.
The request therefore runs on a daemon thread and is abandoned if it overruns. In a
batch of 1,400 that is the difference between one slow record and a job that never
finishes.

NOTE: `skill_router/router.py` on branch `worktree-jev-skill-router` still carries its
own copy of this logic. When that branch merges, point it at this module so there is
one HTTP path rather than two that can drift.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import threading
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_ENDPOINT", "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone")
MODEL = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_MODEL", "jev-latest")
MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024


class JevError(RuntimeError):
    """Anything that stopped us getting a usable answer."""


def api_key() -> str:
    """Env var first, then ~/.claude/typesafe.env.

    The key must keep its `apikey_` prefix. A 401 means the key value is wrong; a 422
    means the request body is. That split is the fastest way to tell which end is at
    fault, and it has cost this project time before.
    """
    key = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY")
    if key and key.strip():
        return key.strip()
    env_file = Path(os.path.expanduser("~")) / ".claude" / "typesafe.env"
    try:
        for line in env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            name, _, value = line.strip().partition("=")
            if name.strip() == "TYPESAFE_API_KEY" and value.strip():
                return value.strip().strip("\"'")
    except OSError:
        pass
    raise JevError(
        "no TYPESAFE_API_KEY in the environment or ~/.claude/typesafe.env"
    )


def system_one(state, questions: dict, key: str, timeout: float = 20.0) -> dict:
    """POST one request and return its `answers` map. Raises JevError on anything else.

    No retries here on purpose: the caller owns retry policy, because what is safe to
    retry in a resumable batch job is not what is safe in a hook.
    """
    body = json.dumps(
        {"state": state, "model": MODEL, "questions": questions}
    ).encode("utf-8")
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        ENDPOINT,
        data=body,
        headers={
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}",
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
        },
        method="POST",
    )

    outcome: dict = {}

    def perform() -> None:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
                raw = response.read(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)
            outcome["data"] = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except BaseException as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - handed back to the caller
            outcome["error"] = error

    worker = threading.Thread(target=perform, daemon=True)
    worker.start()
    worker.join(timeout)
    if worker.is_alive():
        raise JevError(f"wall-clock timeout after {timeout}s")
    if "error" in outcome:
        raise JevError(f"{type(outcome['error']).__name__}: {outcome['error']}")

    payload = outcome.get("data")
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise JevError("response is not an object")
    answers = payload.get("answers")
    if not isinstance(answers, dict) or not answers:
        raise JevError("response carried no answers")
    return answers
